51088082.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant ezrin (unknown origin) by surface plasmon resonance spectrometry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Evaluation of small molecule binding to recombinant ezrin was performed by surface plasmon resonance spectroscopy as follows: A Biacore CM5 sensorchip was initially primed three times with HBS-P (0.01 M HEPES pH 7.4, 0.15 M NaCl, 0.005% v/v Surfactant P20) buffer, followed by 1-ethyl-3-[3-dimethylaminopropyl]carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC) and N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) solutions (720 s). Recombinant ezrin protein was loaded onto the CM5 chip in a pH 5.5 acetate buffer at a rate of 10 μL/min for capturing ~12,000 RU, followed by a 720 s ethanolamine block cycle. A running buffer containing 10% DMSO, 25 mM Tris pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM EGTA, 0.5 mM Na3VO4, 5 mM β-glycerophosphate, 0.01% Triton X-100, 200 mM ATP was used for the binding analysis of inhibitors to recombinant ezrin. As a positive control, compound NSC 668394 was injected at 1.56, 3.125, 6.25, 12.5 and 25.0 μM concentrations to calculate the binding kinetics of the reaction. Each hit molecule from the different structure classes were evaluated independently with NSC 668394 and injected at the concentrations listed above. Mean equilibrium steady state affinities (K_D) and standard deviations were calculated from three independent experiments for each compound.
original_paragraph.Table 1 caption: Binding affinities determined by surface plasmon resonance spectrometry (BIAcore). Kinetics experiments were run in triplicate unless noted. In each kinetics experiment, compound was injected in triplicate at 7 different concentrations, ranging from 0 to 50 μM. Mean K_D values and standard deviations were calculated from three independent experiments for each compound.
original_paragraph.Table 2 caption: Binding affinities determined by surface plasmon resonance spectrometry. Kinetics experiments were run in triplicate unless noted. In each kinetics experiment, compound was injected in triplicate at 7 different concentrations, ranging from 0 to 50 μM. Binding data was correlated to a 1:1 binding mode and mean K_D values and standard deviations were calculated from three independent experiments for each compound.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: DNA intercalation studies with doxorubicin and NSC 668394. Decrease in Hoechst 33258-DNA fluorescence following addition of doxorubicin (■) or NSC 668394 (♦). Excitation at 370 nm and emission at 480 nm in a 0.01 SHE buffered solution. Initial Hoechst 33258 and Type 1 calf thymus DNA concentrations were 5 μM and 100 μL of 1.0 mg/mL, respectively. Fluorescence values are provided as percentages of the maximum.

analyte.concentration_range: 1.56 μM - 25.0 μM (for NSC 668394; other compounds tested in 7 concentrations from 0 to 50 μM)
